title: Living well in Chicago in the 1920s
summary: Her brother set her up in a Chicago house with rooms for Herschel and family, and Ma Rainey and Susie visited.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And then, after he sent me that, they sent me -- I went to Chicago. They put me in a house on 428 Golden (PHONETIC) Avenue and a great big ______. There were seven rooms in the house (unintelligible). He paid it back to me, you know. But at first, he wasn't (unintelligible), you know. See, after Mama died, you know, Buddy didn't do me right. I thought (unintelligible) if he hadn't done it, somebody would have done it and I wouldn't have got ______. So I'm glad that he was the one that done it, because I did get (unintelligible). Buddy sure did fix my room up nice and he had a nice home (unintelligible) two, three rooms, you know.
So you liked that time in Chicago?
When you had that nice home.
That was before you got married?
No, I was married to my husband.

Uh-huh, (inaudible), uh-huh. And I brought Herschel with me. I kept Herschel ______. I give Herschel a room and I had my sister's little baby ______ with me. I give her a room. And then I brought my baby sister here, I gave her a room. Then Buddy had a room and I had a room. Then I had a dining room and kitchen, you know. Then I had a living room.
So you were living good in Chicago?
Uh-huh. But I was young, I didn't (unintelligible) one or two people. I knew Sue and Butter and (unintelligible) some time, you know.
Didn't Ma Rainey come around some time?
Yeah, but she wouldn't come see me, she'd come to see Buddy.
But Sue would come around and get me and we'd go around to Ma's house, you know. (Unintelligible). I was small then and I was real young. But I was real young, real young. I wasn't even 20.
